# Migration - [`--add-exports`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java)

There can be a situation when a module needs to read something that is not
exported by the other module. Consider the following two JAR files as shown in
the following table.

| JAR File     | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies | Main Method |
| ------------ | -------- | --------- | ------------ | :---------: |
| `app.jar`    | Modular  | Named     | `domain.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar` | Modular  | Named     |              |     No      |

The `app.jar` uses a package that is not exported by the `domain.jar` (for
demonstration purposes). We can use the `--add-exports` command line option to
allow the `app.jar` access the `demo.domain` package, defined within the
`domain.jar`.

> ```
> --add-exports module/package=target-module(,target-module)*
> ```
>
> Updates module to export package to target-module, regardless of module
> declaration. The target-module can be `ALL-UNNAMED` to export to all unnamed
> modules.
([reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#extra-options-for-java))

This should be considered as a **temporary solution** until the module is
properly updated to export the packages or the consumer uses other classes
instead.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

   All modules available on the module path

3. Describe the JAR files

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.domain
   ```

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   demo.app@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/app.jar!/module-info.class
   requires demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application will fail to launch because the domain module does not export
   the package required by the application module.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalAccessError: class demo.app.Main (in module demo.app) cannot access class demo.domain.Quote (in module demo.domain) because module demo.domain does not export demo.domain to module demo.app
       at demo.app@1.0.0/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:8)
   ```

   Export the `demo.domain` package from the `demo.domain` module to the
   `demo.app` module using the `--add-exports` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-exports demo.domain/demo.domain=demo.app \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This time the application works and prints the following.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```

   (*Optional*) Load the `app.jar` as an unnamed module (using the
   `--class-path` instead).

   Note that the `--add-exports` is required as the `demo.domain` module does
   not export the `demo.package` module. If the `demo.domain` module exports the
   package, then only the `--add-modules` is required.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --module-path './target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --add-exports demo.domain/demo.domain=ALL-UNNAMED \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   This will produce the same quote.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```
